speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I can see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; to help me understand what is happening inside you, please tell me if your stools are pale, acholic, or clay-colored, and whether your urine or skin has turned yellow. Also, has your mother noticed a "kissing scar" or any dark urine since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the crying worsens with abdominal palpation, do you notice any visible peristaltic waves or a palpable mass in the upper abdomen? Also, has the baby vomited anything that looked like coffee grounds or bilious (green) fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyloric Stenosis

REQUEST IMAGES: Upper Abdominal Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Serum Electrolytes
